transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-15
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes (recording end approx 16:48)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Price (Redwood SE), Lara Ortiz (EdenWorks Head of ML), Tom Becker (Platform Eng), Priya Singh (SRE)

Auto-summary: Align POC scope for pilot focused on inference capacity sizing. Primary goals: prove predictable p95/p99 latency under production-like concurrency with reserved GPUs, validate burst-to-cloud strategy up to 3x traffic, and ensure graceful fallback to smaller models or queued requests when burst fails.

Topics: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, reserved size, burst/fallback policy, telemetry and SLAs, timeline and next steps.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Ethan on the infra side. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Lara (EdenWorks): Hi Maya, thanks. Lara here. We're excited to scope this pilot, want to make sure we capture the right success criteria.
[00:12] Ethan (Redwood SE): Hey all, quick note, I'll focus on the benchmark design and the fallback mechanics — apologies in advance for any audio blips.
[00:19] Tom (EdenWorks): Tom joining, platform lead — we'll be the ones plumbing traffic into the pilot env.
[00:23] Priya (EdenWorks): Priya here, SRE — most interested in p99 latency and how failover behaves.
[00:29] Maya: Great. Quick agenda: 1) agree success criteria, 2) traffic profile and sizing, 3) reserved GPU & burst strategy, 4) fallback policies and metrics, 5) schedule. Sound good?
[00:36] Lara: Yep, go ahead.

[00:45] Ethan: To set expectations, Redwood pilots typically do a 48-hour benchmark with a reserved pool sized to handle baseline plus a burst factor. We capture token cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, concurrency, and system metrics.
[00:55] Lara: Baseline question — our prod traffic today: median concurrency ~85 requests/sec across our two regions, peak spikes to ~250 rps, and avg prompt length is about 350 tokens with responses 150-300 tokens. Does that help sizing?
[01:05] Tom: Also note that 40% of requests are short prompts (under 100 tokens) and 60% heavier. We have KV cache hit rates around 12% currently.

[01:15] Maya: Very useful. For the pilot we'll approximate that distribution. Two sizing approaches: conservative reserved capacity to cover p95 at baseline (so we hit latency SLO without burst), or smaller reserved with larger burst headroom. Which is more important — strict p95 at baseline or cost minimization?
[01:29] Lara: We're leaning toward predictable p95 at baseline now — product team requires <300ms p95 for short prompts and <700ms p95 for heavy prompts. But cost is important for the PoC acceptance criteria too.
[01:40] Priya: Also add that for the SRE bar we'll require observed p99 under 2.2s during sustained baseline, and graceful degradation under burst.

[01:50] Ethan: Ok, so target SLOs: short prompts p95 <300ms, heavy prompts p95 <700ms, p99 <2.2s. We'll design the reserved pool to hit p95 for baseline concurrency of ~85 rps with a safety buffer — usually 20-30%.
[02:06] Tom: How does Redwood calculate that reserved count? Is it GPUs (V100/A100/NX) or vCPU equivalents?
[02:12] Ethan: Good question — our platform sizes by model throughput on the instance/slot type. For example, with an A100-80GB-equivalent slot running quantized Llama-XX variant, we estimate approx 60 tokens/sec per slot for heavy prompts concurrent across ~6 in-flight streams, but it's very model-dependent. For your mix, preliminary recommends 6 slots (reserved) to cover baseline with buffer, plus burst pool in the cloud that can scale to +12 slots.
[02:37] Lara: So reserved 6 and burst up to 18 total? That's kind of in line with our tolerance. What's the cost delta?
[02:44] Maya: We'll provide exact cost scenarios in the playbook, but back-of-envelope reserved 6 will be predictable monthly commit while burst usage billed on-demand. The playbook will show per-token and per-hour comparisons and estimated monthly burn for expected traffic.

[02:58] Priya: On fallbacks — what's on the table? We need automatic graceful fallback when burst isn't available. Options we discussed: queueing requests (with a TTL), fall back to a smaller/faster model for degraded quality, or regional failover. Thoughts?
[03:10] Ethan: All three are supported. We recommend a layered policy: 1) try reserved pool, 2) expand into burst pool (cloud), 3) if burst saturation or cross-region latency would violate SLO, route to smaller model variant (e.g., quantized medium) for degraded quality, 4) if even that can't be served within TTL, return a user-facing "retry later" signal. Policy parameters: queue TTL, max queue depth, and quality threshold.
[03:34] Lara: That sequence seems sensible. We'd like to avoid user-facing failures, so queue TTL of 2s might be okay for interactive flows, but for some async features we can tolerate 15s. We'll mark interactive features as strict.
[03:45] Tom: How do we test the fallback in the benchmark? Simulate burst fill and then deny burst to see degrade path?
[03:51] Ethan: Exactly. We'll run two phases: Phase A (baseline + controlled spikes) with burst allowed; Phase B (burst disabled) to verify fallback path and observe fallbacks to smaller models and queueing behavior. We'll capture ratio of fallbacks, mean quality delta (we'll use simple BLEU-like approximate or embedding distance as a proxy), and user-visible error rates.

[04:10] Maya: Success criteria — I'll propose we require: 1) baseline p95 targets met with reserved sizing, 2) under 3x traffic spike with burst enabled, p95 increases no more than 1.8x and error rate <0.5%, 3) when burst is disabled, fallbacks keep error rate <2% and median quality delta acceptable to PM (we'll ask EdenWorks to define acceptable quality thresholds).
[04:29] Lara: That works. Add cost threshold: pilot must not exceed X% projected monthly cost for production (we'll discuss specific cap offline).

[04:38] Priya: Telemetry — what will Redwood send? We need per-request timing, model variant, slot id, host metrics, and tracing to tie back to our logs.
[04:46] Ethan: We'll provide per-request metadata tokens: request_id, model, variant, slot, start/end timestamps, queue wait, fallback flag, and cost estimate. We can forward traces to your hosted tracing or S3 bucket. We'll also expose a dashboard with p50/p95/p99 and token cost breakdown.
[05:01] Tom: Security — we need SSO, audit logs, SOC2 attestation. Also the pilot needs to run in our VPC for data control. Is VPC pilot possible?
[05:10] Maya: Yes, Redwood Private can run a pilot in your VPC. For speed we can start with hosted reserved in Redwood's region plus strict encryption of payloads, but if you need VPC from day one we can spin up a private pilot — it'll add setup time (usually 2-3 weeks). Which do you prefer?
[05:23] Lara: We prefer VPC but if that delays the benchmark we can do an initial hosted run with strict retention policies and then migrate. PM prefers quicker time-to-bench.
[05:32] Priya: Two things: we'll need KMS integration and audit log access for the pilot.
[05:36] Maya: Noted — we'll include KMS integration steps and sample IAM policies in the security packet.

[05:44] Ethan: On metrics capture — we will record p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens in/out, GPU utilization, queue depth, KV cache hit, and failure flags every 30s. We'll provide the raw CSV and a dashboard.
[05:55] Tom: For the benchmark harness, what load generator should we use? We use internal or can Redwood provide one?
[05:59] Ethan: We have a harness (JMeter-based + custom client) we can run from Redwood's benchmarking rig but we prefer ingesting a sanitized trace you provide so the shape matches your traffic. We can also run synthetic tails to exercise worst-case prompts.

[06:12] Lara: We'll sanitize and send a 7-day trace by Apr 20. Action: Tom to export and remove user PII.
[06:17] Priya: One more — if the reserved pool is underutilized, can we shrink it mid-pilot?
[06:21] Maya: For pilot we allow one resize event; for production reserved is contractual. For the POC we'll flex a bit — we can scale down if you confirm before a change window.

[06:30] Tom: Timeline check — we want bench week Apr 26, can Redwood prep by then?
[06:33] Ethan: Yes. Here's the suggested schedule: Apr 20 receive trace + security docs, Apr 22 confirm model variant and reserved slot type, Apr 26-27 run 48-hour benchmark, Apr 29 deliver report and replay session.
[06:45] Lara: Sounds good.

[06:50] Maya: Quick clarification on model variants — we'll onboard your chosen open model or our recommended quantized variant. Which model do you want to try?
[06:56] Lara: The product team prefers the Llama-XX-13B family (quantized), but we want to test a smaller 7B fallback.
[07:02] Ethan: Perfect — recommended pilot run on the 13B quantized as primary, with 7B quantized as the fallback. We'll measure embedding/semantic delta for quality checks.

[07:13] Priya: Do you have any SLA for pilot runs?
[07:16] Maya: For pilots we provide operational support and an agreed-on runbook; formal SLA comes with Dedicated contracts. But we'll commit to timely support during the benchmark window.

[07:24] Tom: Competitor note — we did a PoC with OtherAI last year and they hit p95 but costs were 2x. Curious how Redwood will show cost parity.
[07:33] Maya: We'll include detailed per-token cost estimates and show how batching, caching and quantization lower token cost. We'll include a comparsion sheet against publicized OtherAI numbers where available.

[07:43] Ethan: One more technical: KV cache — your 12% hit rate helps. If we can pre-warm prefix caching for common flows we'll shave a lot off latency. We'll analyze your trace for good prewarm candidates.
[07:55] Lara: Good. Priya: Anything else on security or regulatory?
[07:59] Priya: We need retention policy not to exceed 30 days for any request logs, and access controls.
[08:04] Maya: We'll include default 30-day retention with options to shorten and will map roles for access.

[08:10] Maya: Ok, recap of agreed next steps: Redwood sends pilot pricing + burst playbook, Ethan will prepare bench harness and metric list, EdenWorks to send sanitized 7-day trace, decide on hosted-first vs VPC by Apr 20. Bench schedule week of Apr 26.
[08:23] Lara: Correct. Please put the playbook link in the recap email.
[08:27] Maya: Will do. Anything else?
[08:30] Tom: Can you also include a sample fallback policy YAML we can review and comment on?
[08:34] Ethan: Yep we'll attach a sample policy and we can iterate.

[08:38] Priya: Last question: how do you quantify quality delta for fallback to 7B?
[08:42] Ethan: We'll compute embedding cosine similarity on a representative set and provide a simple threshold matrix — we'll work with your PM to set acceptance.

[08:50] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the security packet and playbook today.
[08:53] Lara: Thanks Maya and Ethan. Looking forward.
[08:56] Maya: Bye all.

--- End of transcript ---
